hints: Look at the order around the circle and find the small slice labelled cell division, then ask which labelled phase comes immediately before it.
Remember when in the cycle chromosomes need to condense, in early mitosis (prophase) just as cell division is about to start, not during the long growth and DNA copying stages.
walkthrough:
**Read the cell cycle in order**

Think of the circle as a clock going round. The long phases A, B and C are interphase for growth and DNA copying, and the tiny slice is cell division itself.

**Recall when chromosomes become visible**

During most of interphase DNA is loose and invisible as chromatin. It only coils, condenses and becomes visible as chromosomes at the start of mitosis, in prophase.

**Pick the phase just before division**

That condensation must happen right before the cell divides. On the diagram, phase D sits directly before the cell division slice, so D is the correct phase.

options.A: A is the largest slice for G1 growth, when the cell grows and makes organelles and the chromosomes are still loose and invisible.
options.B: B is the S phase for DNA replication, when DNA is being copied as chromatin, not condensed into visible chromosomes.
options.C: C is an earlier interphase growth stage, when the cell is preparing for division but chromosomes have not yet condensed.
options.D: D is immediately before cell division, matching early mitosis (prophase) when chromatin condenses into short, thick, visible chromosomes.
